sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Cuyahoga County?
sections.html:
Three pieces of the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office matter to a property owner. The Appraisal department values every parcel, the Board of Revision hears complaints about those values, and the Treasurer's Office bills the real estate tax and invests the revenue. The Fiscal Officer's department page also lists Real Property for credits and charges, a Budget Commission that sets tax rates, Delinquent Tax Outreach, and a Transfer and Recording office for property records. Recorded documents are available from 1810 forward.

Everything sits at the Cuyahoga County Administrative Building, 2079 East 9th Street in Cleveland. The county's property FAQ places Transfer and Recording on the 4th floor, Appraisal on the 3rd floor, the Treasurer on the 1st floor and the Board of Revision on the 2nd, and gives 216-443-7420 as the number for land records, appraisals and the Fiscal Office.

sections.h2: When and how is Cuyahoga County property tax paid?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is billed twice a year and in arrears, one year behind. The Treasurer's Pay Your Taxes page says taxes accrued in 2025 are due in 2026, in mid-February and mid-August. Manufactured home tax is billed for the current year, with payments due in early March and late August. Owners can sign up for EasyPay to prepay future bills or for E-Billing to receive bills by email or text.

Way to payWhat the Treasurer prints
OnlineE-check has no fee; debit card carries a flat $2.95; credit card is 2.3% with a $1.50 minimum
Phone1-877-738-1212, with an asterisk standing in for each space in the parcel number
In personCashier on the 1st floor at 2079 East 9th Street, open only during collection season in January and February and in July and August
MailPO Box 94547, Cleveland, OH 44101, checks or money orders only
Drop boxOutside the Administrative Building, checks or money orders only

The Treasurer warns mail payers that a postmark shows when the post office machinery processed the envelope, not necessarily the day it was mailed. Because Ohio law relies on the postmark, people paying near a due date are urged to allow extra time, ask for a hand-stamped postmark at the counter, or use another payment method.

sections.h2: What if a Cuyahoga County owner falls behind on the tax?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 323.121 puts a ten percent penalty on the unpaid balance of a late half and adds interest on delinquent taxes at the rate set under section 5703.47. The penalty drops by half when the whole amount comes in within ten days of the deadline. A valid delinquent tax contract stops further interest while it stays in force, and it becomes void if the owner breaks it.

The Treasurer's outreach calendar advertises Last Chance Payment Plan classes for owners who are seeking a third delinquent tax contract, offered online and at the Financial Empowerment Center at 2079 East 9th Street. The Fiscal Officer's department list also names Delinquent Tax Outreach as the unit that helps the Prosecutor and Treasurer collect overdue tax. An owner who wants to sell a house with a balance should phone the Treasurer for the amount owed and ask whether a payment contract is in place, so the title company has the full picture.

sections.h2: How does a Cuyahoga County owner appeal a valuation?
sections.html:
By lodging a complaint with the Cuyahoga County Board of Revision during the window that opens each January 1 and shuts on March 31. The Board's page says the tax year 2025 filing period has closed and the next one runs from January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027. The county's property FAQ adds that a complaint must claim over-valuation, under-valuation, discriminatory valuation, illegal valuation or an incorrect determination of use.

The people who may file are broader than most owners expect. The FAQ lists any owner of taxable real property in the county, the commissioners, the prosecutor, the treasurer, any school board in the county, and the mayor or legislative authority of a municipality with land in the county. Cuyahoga was reappraised in 2024 under Ohio's six-year cycle, and the Fiscal Office page notes that a higher valuation does not by itself mean a higher tax bill.

A residential owner has to back up an opinion of value. The Fiscal Office lists the kinds of evidence the board expects:

  • A full appraisal report completed in the last calendar year
  • Dated photographs showing the property's existing condition
  • Certified contractor estimates for repairs
  • A purchase agreement with its closing statement
  • Certified new construction costs from the builder

Phone the board at 216-443-7195, and its office, on the second floor at 2079 East Ninth Street, keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 4:30. Each complaint is set for a hearing, so the owner arrives with the evidence in hand.

sections.h2: Which tax credits and protections does Cuyahoga County offer?
sections.html:
The Fiscal Office links four resources to its reappraisal page: the homestead exemption, an owner occupancy credit, a military deferment under which property taxes can be deferred, and Property Alerts to protect owners from deed fraud. Each carries its own state form or sign-up, so ask the Fiscal Office which ones fit a house you own but do not live in.

The Fiscal Office's reappraisal page also stresses that an owner contesting value must produce documents, not just a figure. That applies to sellers who bought recently, since the purchase agreement and closing statement are on the evidence list.

When a house sells, the grantor pays the auditor-side conveyance fee under ORC 319.54, set at $1 or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is more. Section 319.202 has the buyer file a statement of value, and any county transfer tax is added. In Cuyahoga County that step runs through the Fiscal Office's Transfer and Recording unit ahead of the recorded copy.

sections.h2: What makes Cuyahoga County different for a seller?
sections.html:
Cuyahoga is a large urban county on the southern shore of Lake Erie. Wikipedia gives its area as 1,246 square miles, of which 457 are land and 788 are water, and calls it the second largest county in Ohio by area. The Cuyahoga River divides it, and part of Cuyahoga Valley National Park lies in the southeast. Lawmakers created the county in 1807, it was organized on May 1, 1810, and Cleveland had been picked as its seat in 1809. Lake, Geauga, Summit, Medina, Lorain and Portage counties touch its borders.

Census QuickFacts estimates 1,232,925 residents for July 1, 2025, which is 2.5% under the 2020 base. The housing side reads:

  • 616,777 housing units, 554,551 households
  • 59.4% of homes owner-occupied
  • A typical owned home worth $195,400 in the 2020 to 2024 figures
  • Rents running at a median of $1,060 a month
  • Median household income of $64,468
  • 1,896 building permits in 2025

The county's population peaked at 1,721,300 in 1970 and has fallen in each census since. A county-wide figure hides large differences between Cleveland, the inner ring and the outer suburbs, so price a particular house from comparable sales or a written offer.

faqs.q: When is Cuyahoga County real estate tax due?
faqs.a: Mid-February and mid-August, according to the Treasurer's Pay Your Taxes page. The tax is billed in arrears, so taxes accrued in 2025 are payable in 2026.

faqs.q: When can I file a valuation complaint in Cuyahoga County?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. The Board of Revision says the next filing period is January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay my Cuyahoga County tax online?
faqs.a: Not for an electronic check. A debit card costs a flat $2.95 and a credit card costs 2.3% with a minimum of $1.50.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late real estate tax payment?
faqs.a: ORC 323.121 sets a ten percent penalty on the unpaid half, cut in half if the whole amount is paid within ten days. Interest is charged on delinquent taxes as well.

faqs.q: Can the county help if I cannot pay all at once?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer lists a delinquent tax payment plan page and holds Last Chance Payment Plan classes for owners seeking a third contract. Call the Treasurer's Office to ask which plan fits.
